chronology.time_unit: engine step (integer scheduler iteration; not wall-clock)
chronology.engine_step_semantics: members = the requests programmed for engine step e (a_r <= e <= a_r + cap_r - 1), each with its request-relative step s = e - a_r and that step's instance segment (component body nodes [lo,hi), segments end at TokenSelect_v1 — X-09's unit) and global gate range; the step's programmed instance set is the union; inside one engine step NO sequence is declared: the step's instances form a DAG multiset per (request, s) whose canonical addresses are structural (component node index = the address-map convention), never an order of events
chronology.convention: continuous scheduling: a request arriving at step a runs its prefill at step a and decode step s at step a+s, no preemption, no chunked prefill; requests co-scheduled in one engine step are addressed by (arrive_step, manifest index) — an addressing key only, not a declared order of their computations (none exists inside a step); there is no programmed data dependency between requests

within_step.criterion: DAG multiset per (request, s) with structural canonical addresses (rev-pm M-0099 (c)); the fold's emission sequence is an encoding of the record, recorded by the checker as layout

chronology.state_dependencies: request-local only: each request's KV cache and previous-token dependencies live inside its component (the request wrapper); no cross-request state, no cache reuse across requests
chronology.observed_time: not represented: observed step indices (fold StepStart) and elapsed time belong to the execution record; agreement with the programmed schedule is the global checker's (gmatch) check, not a builder claim

future_dependent_events.eos_stop: prescribed: the Program computes all cap steps of every request; an execution that stops a request early at EOS leaves the tail programmed-but-unexecuted; the builder does not rebuild from served lengths (rules §2.6)
future_dependent_events.post_eos_lag: LAG = 1 declared: after an EOS stop before the cap exactly 1 more programmed step(s) of the request RUN (active internal computation, fed the EOS; sampled token not served); inactivity starts at a_r + 1

lengths.served_output_len: a_r = output events up to and including the first declared EOS id (eos_token_ids), else cap
lengths.executed_prefix_len: a_r + 1 after an EOS stop before the cap (LAG step(s): active internal computation, sampled token NOT served); a_r on a length stop (a_r == cap; an EOS sampled at the cap is a length stop, no post-EOS row)
lengths.cap_exhaustion: a_r == cap (length stop): specified separately from the EOS stop; never widened by the lag
lengths.eos_set: stop_rule.eos_token_ids, NOT widened by the post-EOS row's discarded sample
lengths.inactivity: positions >= a_r + 1 of an EOS-stopped request are programmed-but-unexecuted (bot in the lifted baseline)
lengths.capacity_covers_lag: cap events per request; a_r <= cap - 1 on an EOS stop, so a_r + LAG <= cap for LAG in {0, 1}
lengths.rule: R17-1 / DP-pad-02 (b); one definition for Build (this Program), GM-01 G6 and the finalizer

address_space: gate index in the canonical layout of the workload root (verity.ir.layout.Circuit); hierarchical path root/node[k]/node[i]... for instances; Input gates first in root-parameter order (the shared group once, then each request's own), then one call node per request in manifest order

engine.enable_chunked_prefill: modelled (a request's prefill rows may span engine steps)

stop_rule.rule: a request may stop before max_tokens only when its last served token is one of eos_token_ids (finish_reason stop/None); stop strings, aborts and drops are not modelled and FAIL G6

moe_construction.population: |Q(P)|: one VU per (token, slot) pair row + router + sum per token
moe_construction.verified_by: GP-01: every component's derive-time target.declared resolves to the same construction and its Program binds that construction's Definitions (refused by name otherwise); the workload digest differs by construction on the same trace; GM-01 reports the label and compares nothing against the record (the record is construction-agnostic)
moe_construction.rule: R17-42 / R17-45 (a): the fused-MoE construction is a declared-and-bound Program static (TargetProfile.moe_construction; indexed-read = MOE-01, padded = MoeFfnFixedL_v1 per token with the hand-authored lift LMoeFfnL_v1 of record); the Build binds the declared construction only, the digest differs by construction on the same trace, GP-01 refuses components of another construction by name; never attested by the record, never inferred from it (moe M-1066 (2a))
